title: Effect of Quorum Sensing Inhibition and Whole-Genome Sequencing Analysis of Pantoea agglomerans Isolated from Ready-to-Eat Braised Chicken
content: Pantoea agglomerans is commonly found in natural and food-processing environments and can drive spoilage in meat products via quorum sensing (QS)-regulated behaviors. We characterized P. agglomerans HJS002, isolated from ready-to-eat braised chicken, and screened natural compounds for QS inhibition. Whole-genome sequencing and LC-MS/MS were used to define genomic features and to identify N-acyl-homoserine lactones (AHLs) signals. The HJS002 genome (one chromosome and four plasmids, 4.18 Mb) encodes genes linked to environmental metabolism (240), ABC transporters (239), two-component systems (140), QS (79), and biofilm formation (44). LC-MS/MS detected three AHLs: C6-HSL, C8-HSL, and 3-oxo-C6-HSL. We compared epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), carvacrol, and eugenol for effects on minimum inhibitory concentration, cell-surface properties, biofilm formation, and production of AHLs and autoinducer-2 (AI-2). At a subinhibitory concentration (64 μg/mL), carvacrol markedly reduced biofilm formation and lowered both AHLs and AI-2 levels, while increasing cell-surface hydrophobicity and aggregation, these effects were significantly greater than those of EGCG and eugenol (p < 0.05). The results identify carvacrol as a promising QS-targeted agent for mitigating P. agglomerans associated spoilage in chicken products and provide genomic context for its persistence in food environments.
